name: Boonaken
description: Boonaken is a lively Dutch Jass-family card game for 4-7 players, famously played for rounds of drinks. Its name is derived from the top three trumps: Boer (Jack), Nel (Nine), and Aas (Ace). It features a unique 'drinking game' structure where players strive to win twice to be safe, while losing twice results in buying the round. It combines standard Jass point-trick mechanics with a competitive auction and card exchange phase.

content.text: Boonaken is a lively Dutch Jass-family card game for 4-7 players, famously played for rounds of drinks. Its name is derived from the top three trumps: Boer (Jack), Nel (Nine), and Aas (Ace). It features a unique 'drinking game' structure where players strive to win twice to be safe, while losing twice results in buying the round. It combines standard Jass point-trick mechanics with a competitive auction and card exchange phase.

Originating in the Dutch pub culture of the Hazerswoude-Rijndijk and Leimuiden areas, Boonaken is a social evolution of Pandoeren. It was specifically designed to find a single loser in a group to facilitate the purchase of drinks.
4 to 7 players playing individually (but forming temporary alliances against the declarer).
32 cards (7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit).
Standard 32-card French pack, score sheet with +/- columns.
Deal 6 cards each. Center cards (widow) are dealt face-up or face-down depending on player count (e.g., 2 face-up for 5 players).

items.text: Misère Bid: A negative bid where the player must lose every trick. No trump suit.
Zwabber: The player must win every trick alone against all opponents.
